HARKESH MANUJA, J.
CM-11290-CI-2018 Prayer in the present application is for condonation of delay of 2242 days in filing the appeal.
Upon notice, no reply has been filed; however, learned State Counsel opposes the prayer made in the application.

I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the contents of the application, which has been supported by one of the applicants-appellants, namely, Attar Singh (appellant No. 1).

sentences.text:
Concededly, the other similarly situated landowners pertaining to the same acquisition proceedings have already been held entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation pertaining to the acquired land falling in same revenue estate, i.e. Village Badshahpur, Tehsil & District Gurgaon, to the tune of Rs. 806/- per square yard, in view of judgment dated 10.12.2015 passed in RFA-2269-2010, titled "Phool Singh and 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:137028 RFA No.
4806 of 2018 (O&M) Neutral Citation No. 2023:PHHC:137028 another Versus State of Haryana and another", which stood attained finality upto the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Based thereupon, applying the principles of parity, besides awarding of just and fair compensation and relying upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of "Ningappa Thotappa Angadi (Dead) through LRs Versus Special Land Acquisition Officer and Another", 2020 (19) SCC 599 as well as in view of the contents of application, the same is allowed and delay of 2242 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned, subject to denial of interest for the delayed period.

sentences.text: MAIN APPEAL

Present appeal has been preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act"), to modify the award dated 26.02.2010 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Gurgaon (hereinafter to be referred as "Reference Court") seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

[2] Briefly, the facts are that in pursuance of Haryana Govt. Notification dated 24.08.2000 issued under Section 4 of the Act, followed by Notification dated 22.08.2001 issued under Section 6 thereof, the land measuring 37.96 acres, including the land of appellants, situated in the revenue estate of Village Badshahpur, Tehsil & District Gurgaon, for development and utilization of residential, commercial and institutional area, Sector-57, Gurgaon, was acquired.

The Land Acquisition Collector, Gurgaon (for short "LAC") vide Award No. 14 dated 21.07.2003, assessed the market value at the per acre rate of Rs. 6,25,000/- for Chahi land, Rs. 4,25,000/- for Bhood &
Banjar land, and Rs. 7,30,000/- for Gair Mumkin land.

[3] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the Act, which were decided vide award dated 26.02.2010 by Reference Court, whereby the market 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:137028 RFA No. 4806 of 2018 (O&M) Neutral Citation No. 2023:PHHC:137028 value of the acquired land was enhanced / assessed @ Rs. 717/-
per square yard, irrespective of the nature of land, besides granting statutory benefits.
[4] It is contended by learned counsel for the appellants that present appeal is squarely covered with the judgment dated 10.12.2015 passed in RFA-2269-2010, titled "Phool Singh and another Versus State of Haryana and another", arising out of the same notification, vide which the land of appellants had been acquired.
[5] Learned State Counsel is not in a position to controvert the above factual position; however,
opposes the payment of interest for the period, the appellants failed to approach this Court after the decision of Reference Court.

sentences.text: [7] From the records, it is apparent that the present appeal is squarely covered with the judgment dated 10.12.2015 passed in case of Phool Singh and another (supra), which is arising out of the same acquisition / Notification dated 24.08.2000 covering the same revenue estate i.e. Village Badshahpur, Tehsil & District Gurgaon, whereby the landowners have been held entitled for the modified / enhanced amount of compensation @ Rs. 806/- per square yard.

For reference, the relevant paras-27 & 28 of judgment dated 10.12.2015 passed in case of Phool Singh and another (supra) reads as under:-
" 27.

To sum up, the landowners are held entitled to compensation as under:
Rates per square yard in Rs.
(i) For the notification dated 1,759/-
24.8.2000 pertaining to revenue estates of Wazirabad and Samaspur 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:137028 RFA No. 4806 of 2018 (O&M) Neutral Citation No. 2023:PHHC:137028 (ii) For the notification dated 1,216/-
24.8.2000 pertaining to revenue estates of Tigra and Ghatta (iii) For the notification dated 806/-
24.8.2000 pertaining to revenue estates of Amarpur Nagli, Badshahpur and Ghasola (iv) For the notification dated 2,403/-
9.6.2003 pertaining to revenue estates of Wazirabad and Samaspur (v) For the notification dated 1,662/-
9.6.2003 pertaining to revenue estates of Tigra and Ghatta 28.
The landowners shall also be entitled to all statutory benefits available to them under the Act.

"
[7.1] Based upon the above, applying the principle of parity, besides award of just and fair compensation, the landowners / appellants being similarly situated are held entitled for grant of similar amount of compensation as has been awarded to other landowners vide judgment dated 10.12.2015 in case of Phool Singh and another (supra), alongwith all other statutory benefits and interest thereupon as provided under the Act, except payment of interest for the period the appellants did not approach this Court after passing of Reference Court's Award.
